name: Gustave Courbet
findings: Uses dark jungle green 2.3x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 757 paintings here).
Uses dark olive brown 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 757 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, camo green turns up as a small accent in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.1x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, metallic blue turns up as the lightest note in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 3.5x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, prout's brown turns up as the shadow in 53% of the paintings that hold it, 2.0x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Pairs buff orange with ochre yellow more than chance would predict (3 of 757 paintings here).
Pairs alice blue with columbia blue more than chance would predict (3 of 757 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark jungle green, dark olive brown) covers 73% of his paintings here.
